# Reviewed false positives of tools/check_no_secrets.py (format: RULE path[:line]).
# An entry that suppresses nothing is reported by the scan, so this list cannot rot.
#
# The requirement lock maps requirement ids to SHA-256 hashes; ids such as M-AUTH-nn contain the
# word "AUTH" and a hash looks like a literal value.  The file is generated by
# `python -m tools.gie_registers lock` and holds no credential.
SC002 specifications/requirements_lock.json
#
# test_results.json (evidence of the review package, generated by `python -m tools.ci`) lists the
# ids of the secret scanner's own parametrised tests; those ids quote the fixture templates of
# the scanner (a name followed by a brace placeholder).  The file is never written by hand.
# junit.xml of the same run is deliberately NOT committed: it repeats those fixtures in several
# more forms and carries long base64 runs (Hypothesis statistics); it stays a CI artifact.
SC002 reviews/session_00/evidence/test_results.json
